title: The Missing Half of the Recipe

scenes.title: Room Four Rings Twice
scenes.summary: Room 4's desk buzzer gives its signature double ring, and F3 brings the old green cloth botanical book downstairs to inspect with F1 and M1.
scenes.intro: Early Sunday afternoon at {SHOW}, the brass front-desk buzzer suddenly gives two crisp rings in a row. {F1} and {M1} look up from the reservation ledger just as {F3} comes down the wooden stairs carrying a worn green cloth book. Listen first.
story: M1
Buzz-buzz on a quiet Sunday—that double ring is definitely Room Four.
F1
Right on cue! Look who is coming down the stairs with a green book!
F3
I pressed the bell once upstairs, {M1}, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
M1
If Room Four ever rang only once, madam, I would think it was broken.
F3
Here is the cloth-bound garden herb book from the second-hand bookshop shelf on {STREET}!
F1
Look at the gold leaf stamped on the faded green cover: Courtyard Herbs and Blossoms.
M1
Check inside the front cover first—old neighbours always wrote their street number there.
F3
Good eye, {M1}! Pencilled in the corner is our exact house number from thirty years ago!
F1
This book actually belonged to {M2} and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
M1
Turn the pages gently over the desk blotter so nothing dry slips onto the floor.
F3
Wait—the book falls open all by itself near chapter seven on summer mint!
F1
Let us carry it straight to {F2} in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
scenes.outro: Stamped with their own house number from thirty summers ago, the green botanical book falls open at the summer mint chapter! See you next time.

scenes.title: Between the Mint Leaves
scenes.summary: In Room 9, F3 lifts the missing bottom half of the berry-and-almond cake recipe from between pressed mint leaves, though an old raindrop blurred the final line.
scenes.intro: On the sunlit table inside Room 9, {F2} lays the top half of the torn recipe card beside the open green botanical book while {F3} and {M2} lean over the pressed herb pages. Let us listen in first.
story: F3
Look right between these two dry sprigs of garden mint and lemon balm.
F2
There is a torn cream card tucked flat against the spine of the book!
M2
Slide it beside the top half from the tin capsule, {F2}—do the edges match?
F2
Every tiny paper fibre lines up like two halves of a broken teacup!
F3
Read the baking instructions aloud so I can copy them cleanly, {F2}.
F2
Fold whole berries gently into the almond batter and bake forty minutes until golden.
M2
Wonderful! That sounds simple enough—why did you squint at the bottom line, {F2}?
F2
Because one big raindrop hit the blue ink right on the secret warm glaze!
F3
Let me look through my glasses: Brush warm cake with two spoons of... blue smudge!
M2
Blue smudge is not an ingredient sold at the Saturday market, {F3}!
F2
Do not panic, boss; we know the cake base, so my kitchen will test three glazes!
M2
Three test cakes on a Sunday afternoon? Now THAT is historical research I support!
scenes.outro: The torn card fits together cleanly, leaving only one raindrop-smudged secret glaze for {F2} and her oven to solve! See you next time.

scenes.title: Three Small Baking Tins
scenes.summary: In the café kitchen, F2 puts aprons on M4 and F1 to bake three small test cakes with three different glazes.
scenes.intro: Fifteen minutes later in the lively café kitchen, {F2} lines up three small round baking tins on the wooden counter while {M4} and {F1} tie clean white aprons around their waists. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F2
Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?
M4
Washed twice, Chef! I brought two baskets of ripe red berries and sweet almonds.
F1
How are we going to solve the smudged blue ink at the bottom, {F2}?
F2
We divide one batch of almond berry batter evenly across three small round tins.
M4
Smart! Same cake inside every tin, with a different warm glaze brushed on top!
F1
What are our three candidate glazes for the great afternoon taste test?
F2
Tin One gets tart lemon juice, Tin Two gets crunchy raw sugar, Tin Three waits.
M4
Why does Tin Three have to wait while One and Two go in first?
F2
Because a good baker learns from the first two mistakes before crowning a winner!
F1
Who is brave enough to serve as our strict, honest Chief Judge today?
M4
Only one person in {SHOW} never flatters anybody, even when dessert is free.
F2
Go fetch {M1} and his sharp pencil—the ovens are hot!
scenes.outro: Three round tins slide toward the warm oven, and {M1} is drafted as the toughest cake judge on {STREET}. See you next time.

scenes.title: Batch One Is Too Sour
scenes.summary: After M2 measures the lemon glaze for Batch One without his reading glasses, M1 takes one bite and declares it sour enough to polish brass.
scenes.intro: Golden steam rises in the café corner as Tin One comes out of the oven. {M2} proudly brushes his own lemon glaze across the top while {F2} hands a small fork to {M1}. Listen first.
story: M2
Stand back and admire Batch One—glazed personally by the owner of {SHOW}!
F2
You measured two small teaspoons of lemon juice plus sugar, right, {M2}?
M2
Two big soup ladles of pure lemon juice for bold, unforgettable summer flavour!
F2
{M2}! Soup ladles?! Where were your reading glasses when you read the spoon size?!
M2
Wait—too late, {M1} already put a full forkful into his mouth!
M1
Give me one quiet moment while my cheeks try to unpucker themselves.
F2
Here is a glass of cold water, {M1}—what is your official pencil score?
M1
The almond crumb is tender, the berries are sweet, and the top melts brass.
M2
Melts brass?! Surely a refreshing citrus zing deserves at least seven points!
M1
I am writing three out of ten, plus a warning label for the front desk.
F2
Thank you for your sacrifice, Judge; {M2} is officially retired from spoon duty!
M2
Hmph! Wait until you see how crunchy {M4} made Batch Number Two!
scenes.outro: Two soup ladles of straight lemon juice earn Batch One three points and a brass-polishing warning from {M1}. See you next time.

scenes.title: Batch Two Crunches Loudly
scenes.summary: M4 unveils Batch Two with a heavy toasted sugar top so hard that his brother M3 jokes he could use it to tile a courtyard roof.
scenes.intro: Five minutes later, {M4} proudly sets Tin Two on the wooden cooling board while his younger brother {M3} steps into the café corner sniffing the sweet caramel air beside {F2}. Let us listen in first.
story: M4
Step right up, little brother! Smell that toasted brown sugar crust on Tin Two!
M3
It smells like a street festival, {M4}, though the top looks surprisingly shiny.
F2
How many spoons of coarse sugar did you sprinkle under the hot grill, {M4}?
M4
Enough to give every slice a satisfying crisp snap when your fork goes down!
M3
Let me press my dessert fork gently right in the middle... tap, tap, clang!
F2
Oh dear—a cake is not supposed to ring like the front-desk bell, {M4}!
M3
Speaking professionally as an architect, we could roof the bicycle shed with Batch Two.
M4
Hey! Break through the top window and taste the warm almond cake underneath!
M3
Mmm, underneath that sugar helmet, the berries and ground almonds are delicious!
F2
So lemon alone is too sour, and dry sugar alone turns into courtyard stone.
M4
What soft, shining glaze could possibly be hiding beneath that blue ink smudge, {F2}?
F2
Bring me that green botanical book again—our noses might read better than our eyes!
scenes.outro: Batch Two could survive a hailstorm on a roof, sending {F2} back to the old botanical book for one more clue! See you next time.

scenes.title: Smelling the Pressed Page
scenes.summary: Holding the smudged recipe card up to the Room 9 window light with F3, F2 spots a tiny orange-blossom sketch and smells wildflower honey and sweet orange peel.
scenes.intro: Inside quiet Room 9, {F2} and {F3} hold the thirty-year-old smudged card and the open botanical book beside the sunny glass panes. Listen first.
story: F3
Tilt the smudged card slightly toward the afternoon sun, {F2}—do you see the first letter?
F2
Two spoons of warm H... and then a round little sketch beside the ink blot!
F3
That tiny round fruit with three pointed leaves is not a lemon—it is an orange!
F2
Wait—warm H plus grated sweet orange peel! Could H stand for wildflower honey?!
F3
Smell the paper right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.
F2
Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
F3
Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or rock hard!
F2
And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering {M1}!
F3
Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
F2
Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange zest, and toasted almond flakes!
F3
Tin Three is still warm on the stove rack—go brush it right now, Chef!
F2
Do not move from that piano bench, {F3}; the real cake is five minutes away!
scenes.outro: Sunlight and a baker's keen nose unlock the thirty-year smudge: warm honey, sweet orange zest, and toasted almond flakes! See you next time.

scenes.title: Ten Out of Ten in Pencil
scenes.summary: F2 serves Tin Three brushed with warm honey and orange zest; M1 eats in silence, writes ten out of ten in his paper ledger, and asks for a second slice.
scenes.intro: Back at the café counter, {F2} slices warm Tin Three, its top glistening with golden honey, fine orange zest, and toasted almond flakes. {F1} holds her breath as {M1} picks up a clean fork. Listen first.
story: F1
Here goes Judge {M1} with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
F2
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
M1
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
F1
He took a second bite! {F2}, he did not make the brass-polish face!
F2
Well, {M1}? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
M1
Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, {F1}.
F1
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
F2
YES! Ten out of ten in {M1} pencil is worth three gold medals!
M1
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
F1
Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mr Tough Judge!
F2
Eat all you want, {M1}, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!
M1
Keep baking like this, {F2}, and half of {CITY} will line up outside our gate.
scenes.outro: Batch Three earns a historic ten out of ten in {M1}'s paper ledger—plus a second slice for strict safety testing! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Red Star Upstairs
scenes.summary: Sharing cake in the courtyard, M3 compares the four-card puzzle map to the second-floor wooden balcony and spots an old brass lantern ring right where the red star points.
scenes.intro: Carrying plates of the winning berry-and-almond cake out under the courtyard shade tree, {F1}, {M1}, and {M3} look up from the four-card map puzzle toward the second-floor wooden balcony. Listen first.
story: M3
Stand right beside table one and match the four-card drawing to our upstairs wall.
F1
There is the wooden balcony outside the second-floor landing—right where the red star sits!
M1
Squint under the left corner beam of that balcony railing, {M3}; what do you see?
M3
Hold on—there is a forged iron ring bolted straight into the heavy oak post!
F1
And look at the trunk of our courtyard shade tree—a matching ring high up!
M1
Now the mapmaker note makes total sense: they strung festival lanterns overhead between those rings!
F1
High rooftop-to-tree lanterns shining down over all twenty-eight seats on Saturday night!
M3
Wait—have you checked the weekend weather forecast for Friday and Saturday afternoon, {M1}?
M1
Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
F1
Paper lanterns plus strong afternoon wind? That sounds like an adventure waiting to happen!
M3
Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
M1
Bring my wooden ladder at nine sharp—this courtyard is going to glow like daylight!
scenes.outro: With the thirty-year cake recipe complete, eyes turn upward to the second-floor balcony—and Friday's approaching wind! End of Episode 3—see you in Episode 4!
